result.reason: The operative language reaches the preferred position: Sparkling may assign without consent to affiliates and qualifying transaction successors; Garman requires consent for other assignments, subject to a reasonableness standard, and may never assign to a Sparkling competitor. It creates no termination right upon Sparkling’s change of control. The cross-reference in Section 20(c) appropriately reconciles the customer-side restriction while preserving the separate restrictions on transfer, lease, export and sublicensing. The additions of notice, reorganization and unreasonable delay are conventional and do not materially exceed or undermine the playbook position.
